newsitem.title: FINLAND: SUOMI'S POHJOLA SHARES CANNOT BE CANCELLED - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: SUOMI'S POHJOLA SHARES CANNOT BE CANCELLED - PAPER.

text.p: Jouni Sarkijarvi, a member of insurer Suomi's supervisory board, said shares representing Suomi's 39 percent stake in insurer Pohjola cannot be cancelled, daily Helsingin Sanomat reported on Wednesday.
"Annulling the shares is not possible," the newspaper quoted Sarkijarvi as saying. A cancellation would mean a transfer of the capital of Suomi insurance policy-holders to Pohjola, he said.
Pohjola has announced plans to incorporate Suomi into Pohjola. One part of this plan was to cancel Suomi's shares in the insurer.
If the shares cannot be cancelled, Suomi would have to sell its Pohjola shares if the restructuring plans are carried out, the paper said.

The restructuring would then put 25 percent of Pohjola shares, and 39 percent of votes, up for sale. Helsingin Sanomat quoted retired Suomi vice president Aimo Narakka as saying that Suomi's stake could be worth "at least 10 billion markka."

The paper said Pohjola's market capitalisation was currently 5.6 billion markka. Narakka said, however, that the value of Suomi's holding in Pohjola could be higher "if for example Skandia and a few other allies bought the shares."
On May 6, mutual Suomi's representatives meeting will decide whether to sell its Salama life-insurance subsidiary to Pohjola, as proposed by the latter as part of the restructuring.
According to Narakka, Pohjola would offer to buy Salama for 600-700 million markka, Helsingin Sanomat said, quoting Narakka as saying this was half of what would be needed.
